cohort: 283 pregnant women at a tertiary hospital in Southern Odisha, India, with 15 having subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) and 268 being euthyroid.
finding: Subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) in pregnancy was associated with several adverse outcomes, including placental abruption (20%), preterm delivery (20%), spontaneous abortion (6.7%), PROM (6.7%), PIH (6.7%), and IUGR (6.7%), although the majority of births were viable (93.3%) with normal birth weights (>2.5kg, 77%) and good APGAR scores (>3 at 5 minutes, 93.3%).
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed in 27% of SCH cases and vaginal delivery in 73%.
birth_weight: Majority of babies had a birth weight above 2.5 kg (77%).
